findings.where: Header nav 'Destinations' (#destinations) and 'How we rank' (links to this page); footer 'Privacy', 'Terms', 'How we rank', 'Report content' (all link to this page)
findings.fault: Every nav and footer link except the email address goes nowhere. 'Destinations' points to an anchor that has no section on this page, and the other four reload the same guide. A visitor who wants another destination, the ranking method, or the legal pages gets nothing.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker who wants to compare Canggu with other spots, or check how Manta ranks before trusting it. 'Rankings and scoring methods are published' is a product principle, and here the link that should prove it is dead.

findings.where: 'Good for' section: the 13 pills (First-time surfers … Sunsets)
findings.fault: Static facts are drawn as tappable filter chips, with filled pills, heavy coloured outlines and some in link-like colours. Per parts.txt none of them can be acted on. They also take hues the palette doesn't have (purple, magenta, pink) and coral-family fills that are kept for the one CTA. Each pill gets a random fill and a random clashing border, so by similarity they suggest categories that mean nothing.
findings.who_objects: A phone visitor will tap 'Remote workers' or 'Budget' expecting to filter hostels, and nothing happens. The brand owner objects to coral and off-palette colours used as decoration in a scannable area, and to the rainbow noise it creates.

findings.fault: This one heading is set in italic turquoise with an underline, which is the link signifier, but it's static (p5). The other section headings ('Surf', 'Good for') are plain ink, so headings of the same kind get two treatments and one of them looks like a link.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who taps 'Vibe' expecting more detail gets nothing. A reader scanning the headings sees one oddly loud heading with no reason for the emphasis.

findings.where: Coming-soon announcement block, at the end of the content (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The interior announcement is set on a saturated crimson ground. The rules file reserves the ink night ground for this block, and red reads as an error or alert. Inside it, the text is held to about half the box width on desktop, which leaves a large empty red field to the right.
findings.who_objects: A visitor reads a neutral 'listings coming soon' note as a warning that something went wrong. The brand owner objects that a named, bounded ink context has been replaced by an alarm colour close to `danger`.

findings.where: H1 'Best Hostels in Canggu' against the whole page body
findings.fault: The headline promises a list of the best hostels, but the page has none. The only admission is a note at the very bottom. The headline is also in title case, against the sentence-case rule.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker arriving from search for 'best hostels Canggu' scrolls looking for hostels, finds only general guide text, and feels misled. This undercuts the honesty the brand claims.

findings.where: Body text throughout: intro paragraph, Surf, Vibe, What to look for, announcement block (worst on phone)
findings.fault: Paragraphs are fully justified. At phone width this opens wide rivers of space, for example 'MantaHostels   is   launching   across' and 'workers   and   long-stay'. Rough word spacing slows reading.
findings.who_objects: A phone reader, the primary user often reading mid-transit, stumbles over uneven gaps in short lines.

findings.fault: It's set as a small, letter-spaced uppercase eyebrow, while the sibling sections 'Surf' and 'Good for' are sentence-case headings. The one section that answers the brief's second question (what to look for in a hostel) looks weakest in the outline.
findings.who_objects: A scanning visitor reads it as a label rather than a section and may skip the most practical advice on the page.

findings.where: Page top and first screen (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The destination page has no hero zone, though the rules file makes destination-page top banners a loud marketing zone. There is no turquoise ground, no illustration and no energy, only a sand page with left-aligned text. The first screen offers no action and no next step.
findings.who_objects: The brand owner, for whom 'sterile' is the named enemy on exactly this kind of surface. A visitor gets no feel of a beach town and nothing to do next.

findings.where: Desktop layout: text column against the 'Good for' chip row and the announcement block
findings.fault: The text runs in a narrow column on the left with the right half of the page empty, while the chips and the red block stretch to full width. The parts don't share one column edge, so the page looks unbalanced and unfinished.
findings.who_objects: A desktop visitor sees a lopsided page that looks like a broken template, which costs first-visit trust.

findings.where: End of page, before the footer
findings.fault: The guide ends with no route onward. There is no link to other Bali destinations and no way to hear when Canggu listings go live, so the visitor's only option is to leave.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker planning their next hop who liked the guide has nowhere to go, and Manta loses them before launch.

findings.fault: The line breaks after 'How we rank ·', leaving a stray separator dot at the end of the first line.
findings.who_objects: Few would notice, but it reads as a careless detail in the footer.
